record.title: Lean formalization reports global weak-solution existence for unforced 2D Navier–Stokes
record.summary: A 27 September 2026 preprint reports a Lean 4 formalization of the Galerkin construction for global Leray–Hopf weak solutions of unforced two-dimensional Navier–Stokes on arbitrary bounded open domains with no-slip boundaries. It also states a finite-horizon forced result on rectangles. The linked public repository identifies PDEIdeas.Paper and documents a lake build command. These are author-reported formalization and artifact details; the research desk has not independently built or audited the code.

It also states a finite-horizon forced result on rectangles. The linked public repository identifies PDEIdeas.Paper and documents a lake build command. These are author-reported formalization and artifact details; the research desk has not independently built or audited the code.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report the formalization in arXiv:2609.33033v1 and link a public source repository. No independent clean build, declaration/axiom audit or semantic proof review was performed in this activation.
technical.compute_or_cost: No compute or service-cost comparison is reported or assessed.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public arXiv v1 text states Theorem 2.1: for unforced 2D Navier–Stokes on a bounded open domain with no-slip boundary conditions, it formalizes a global weakly continuous velocity path with the weak equation and energy inequality on finite horizons. Theorem 2.3 states a finite-horizon forced result for a rectangle under its stated admissible-forcing assumptions. The repository README names PDEIdeas.Paper and gives `lake exe cache get` and `lake build` commands.
technical.implementation_status: Public preprint and linked Lean repository are available; independent build status unknown.
technical.mechanism: The paper describes a Lean 4 development formalizing the Galerkin construction, compact spectral coordinates, transport cancellation, two-dimensional Ladyzhenskaya estimates, space-time compactness and passage to a Leray–Hopf weak-solution limit.
technical.novelty: Machine-checking a long Galerkin/compactness construction for the stated 2D weak-existence scope and exposing a repository artifact.
technical.regime: Unforced 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes on arbitrary bounded open planar domains with no-slip boundary conditions, plus the paper’s finite-horizon forced rectangular-domain case. Not 3D smoothness or uniqueness.
technical.reproducibility: The repository documents Lean 4.30.0-rc1 and a mathlib revision in its paper-linked setup; this activation did not pin a source commit, build the project, or inspect theorem declarations/axioms.
technical.strongest_baseline: The classical Galerkin existence theory for two-dimensional Navier–Stokes; the contribution tracked here is formalization and reusable proof-assistant infrastructure, not a new existence theorem.

brief.title: Lean formalization reports global weak-solution existence for unforced 2D Navier–Stokes
brief.why_it_matters: Formalizing the Galerkin, compactness and energy-inequality route creates a machine-checkable reference and reusable Lean infrastructure for PDE formalization. The mathematical existence result itself is established 2D theory. This development does not concern smooth 3D regularity, the 3D Millennium problem, or OpenAI’s separate forced-blowup claim.
